tasks.query: I have a small exact description that predicts passage times through a directed stochastic network. Can I turn it into a finite nonnegative-rate process with a specified ceiling on every hidden clock, and what happens at zero eliminated population?

I know the complete distribution of waiting times and also the complete distribution of accumulated event intensity. Is that enough to predict a rate intervention, or do I need to know which two observations came from the same trial?
Each observed output leaves exactly two possible original inputs. Must one affine bit of the original input always distinguish those two, and can an efficiently decoded nonlinear bit do better?

A coherent storage fault hardly changes the source output in my chosen test. Can the retained measurement record still dominate the operation error, and can I replace the fault by a stochastic Pauli channel?

In a finite graded quantum simulation I discard high excitation sectors. Is small population outside the cutoff at the final time sufficient to bound a low-bandwidth observable, or must paths that leave and return be counted?

A probability-based formula controls waiting for a rare complete configuration. May I replace the singleton by a set of configurations and substitute the normalized event indicator into the same Green function identity?

I want to test many structural rewrites of a modular tensor factorization without rebuilding every derivative matrix. Can a quotient of the old tangent image decide whether a plus move removes the first lifting obstruction?

I have tagged arrival counts and a time-resolved histogram of total vacant sites, but no microscopic pair images or fitted hidden generator. Can graph geometry give bounded predictions for a finite change in arrival rates?
Which acquired physical catalyst experiment proves that the new coarse receiver improves product yield over every ordinary method?
